goals: Preserve C12's C9-derived nested shulker routing, source accounting, ordering, capacity, and optional CSR affinity while making only the survival QSN action placement stable and idempotent.

Keep a physically populated carried vanilla shulker out of every ordinary QSN loose-source discovery and movement path for its entire action while preserving C16 direct-content draining under the real user rules.
Keep a CSR-reserved nested slot owned by its exact item-and-components reservation even while its physical stack is empty.
Place the survival QSN action as the upper member of the shared 18px bottom-right utility stack without a Notebook runtime dependency.
Preserve accepted C8 and rollback C6 provenance separately from retained C9 and rejected C10/C11 historical evidence.
scope: Current C15 is a C12-derived compatibility-sidecar placement-stability correction, not a continuation of C10 or C11 implementation or behavior. C10 and C11 remain historical records only.

On a physically empty nested slot, C15 preserves C12's C9 public CSR reservation matcher: a matching reservation is eligible, a mismatching active reservation is blocked, and only an unreserved empty slot is generic capacity.

C15 leaves existing physical-stack merging, nested discovery, parent-first ordering, reservation creation and maintenance, container scanning, source rules, transactional writeback, and C9 identity semantics unchanged.

C15 changes only the survival InventoryScreen QSN action placement: its existing upstream QuickStackIconButton is explicitly recognized as QSN-owned when the production reservation seam scans Screens.getWidgets(screen), so the action cannot collide with itself. Every unrelated visible widget remains a collision; the C14 18x18 Minecraft Button chrome, crisp glyph, tooltip, primary/right-click callbacks, and exact utility-stack geometry are unchanged. Controlled unit and Fabric GameTest evidence is not Minecraft gameplay runtime evidence.

C13 is retained as immutable historical release evidence but is not a viable client artifact: the user-supplied Minecraft 26.2 launch failed before menu initialization because its chrome mixin could not resolve that shadow. C14 is immutable historical evidence with a user-reported survival InventoryScreen placement failure: with QSN 0.4.0 loaded, the otherwise correct action alternated frame-to-frame between adjacent 22px utility slots. That report does not assert a Test Instance Manager deployment or managed Workbench transition. C15 is ACTIVE, NOT_DEPLOYED, and RUNTIME_UNTESTED.

C17 is a narrow C16 successor. At QSN action start it recognizes vanilla BlockItem -> ShulkerBoxBlock carriers with at least one non-empty physical DataComponents.CONTAINER slot, overlays a transient locked SourceRules entry only for native loose discovery/movement, and keeps C16's carried source snapshot on the original user rules. Thus a carrier drained empty this press stays put until the next press; physically empty shulkers remain native QSN items. C16 user-reported/external feedback confirmed carried-source draining worked but reported that a populated matching carrier could be moved as an ordinary outer item. Neither feedback nor C17 controlled validation implies a Test Instance Manager deployment or promotion.

exclusions: Container Slot Reservations, Carried Container Auto-Routing, Matcha × Stack to Nearby Chests Compatibility, Inventory Search, Block Geometry Extensions, Nibaru, Clutter No More, Quick Stack Nearby, and every other nearby-routing or inventory project retain their own identities, source, artifacts, controls, and behavior ownership.

No CSR reservation mutation, persistence, user interface, container-support policy, or classification logic is reimplemented; C8 consumes only CSR's public read-only reservation API when the provider is loaded.

No Stack to Nearby Chests implementation, Matcha-specific QSN adapter, general Inventory Search patch, carried-container routing, nested-container routing, registry-name parsing, fuzzy material equivalence, item conversion, or custom existing-stack merge is owned here.

C15 is a C12-derived compatibility-sidecar artifact. It does not carry forward C10/C11's integrated upstream-QSN implementation or behavior, and it does not bundle external QSN, CSR, Inventory Extended, Clutter No More, BGE, Nibaru, Minecraft, or Fabric JARs.

C8 mirrors the exact audited QSN 0.4.0 package-private maximum-stack helper through its current Container#getMaxStackSize delegate because attempted Java-package and Mixin invokers were not runtime-safe; a future QSN helper change requires seam re-audit.
Controlled JUnit and Fabric GameTest results are build/static evidence, not Minecraft gameplay runtime validation.

Lifecycle is ACCEPTED because exact current C8 was promoted into accepted Stack v17 and no longer occupies a Test Slot; C6 is rollback, C4 remains distinct historical passing provenance, and C7's independent failure remains separate.

C8 has controlled validation and exact serialized deployment/promotion evidence. The user's later combined CSR/QSN report was recorded only as an aggregate C8 PASS with no inferred row-level observations; the earlier narrow zero-physical-quantity observation remains preserved in history, and the protected gameplay instance remained untouched.
